title: Canvas
description: Canvas, the canvas painting look, is a photographic subject wearing oil: visible bristle, canvas tooth, thicker paint in the lights, eyes that still look. It is not a slider named oil: brushwork has direction and weight.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Portraits that should feel made by hand, credits, a memory: you still compose a shot of a person, then the stock becomes paint. The camera is usually a portrait distance, locked, so stroke direction can be read.
If you cannot see a stroke, it is a grade, not canvas. It is the wrong tool when you wanted unfinished line, optical dabs, or wet process.
Those are sketch, Monet muse, and hand-paint. A luxury ad may want magazine instead.

blocks.text: 50mm to 85mm, eye height, lock-off. North window or a large soft source, painter's studio logic.

blocks.text: A handmade portrait, a credit still, a memory that should feel painted and finished. Do not use it as a smooth painterly filter with no tooth.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: Smooth plastic painterly with no tooth, or a mash with Sketch line. The tell is no stroke.
Fix it: bristle, canvas weave, thicker paint in the lights, a face that still looks.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Canvas in film?
A photographic shot whose stock is oil paint: visible bristle, canvas tooth, a face that still looks. It is material, not a mood word.
Canvas vs Monet Muse
Canvas shows the object of painting: bristle and tooth. Monet muse dissolves the scene into optical dabs. If you see weave, you are on canvas. If you see broken color mixing, you wanted Monet muse.
When should I use Canvas?
Handmade portraits, credits, memory. Skip unfinished sketches, wet process shots, and smooth filters with no stroke.
How do I prompt Canvas for AI image or video?
Portrait lens, window key, then: Canvas treatment of [Subject], visible brush, oil tooth, a painting that still has a face. Demand bristle and tooth. Keep the eyes.
